cleanIntro: The Shield Plus will not come apart until the yellow sear deactivation lever is pushed down into the magazine well — that step is the whole difference between this pistol and every earlier Shield. Deep Clean is the magazine.

steps.title: This book is for the SHIELD Plus and SHIELD X only
steps.action: Confirm your pistol is a SHIELD Plus (or a SHIELD X). Smith & Wesson publishes separate manuals for the M&P SHIELD and for the M&P SHIELD EZ pistols, and this one is not written for either of them.
steps.prose: It matters mechanically, not just administratively: the original Shield strips without touching the sear deactivation lever this pistol has, and the EZ has a grip safety that changes how the slide comes off. Following the wrong book on a Shield Plus means either forcing a slide that will not move or reaching into a frame that has nothing to reach for.
steps.quote: NOTE: There are separate manuals for the M&P SHIELD® and the M&P® SHIELD® EZ® pistols. These manuals are available free upon request or via download from www.smith-wesson.com
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Cover page, p.1

steps.title: Determine which features are present on your specific pistol
steps.action: Work out what your particular pistol carries before you go on. Across the SHIELD Plus and SHIELD X line the features that vary include a manual thumb safety, a magazine disconnect safety, a ported barrel and slide, and one of several loaded chamber indicators.
steps.prose: Two of those change the strip directly. A thumb safety up in SAFE locks the slide, so an owner who does not know theirs has one will decide the pistol has seized. A magazine disconnect means the trigger will not release with the magazine out, which matters if you are used to dropping the hammer as part of a routine — on this pistol it may simply not happen, and that is the safety working, not a fault.
steps.quote: YOU MUST DETERMINE WHICH FEATURES ARE PRESENT ON YOUR SPECIFIC SMITH & WESSON® FIREARM AND HOW THOSE FEATURES AFFECT OPERATION OR HANDLING. VARIOUS MODELS OF THE SHIELD® PLUS AND SHIELD X™ PISTOLS ARE FITTED WITH DISTINCT FEATURES, WHICH MAY INCLUDE: A MANUAL THUMB SAFETY, A MAGAZINE DISCONNECT SAFETY, A PORTED BARREL AND SLIDE
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Model & Features Identification, WARNING, p.13
steps.warn: You must determine which features are present on your specific Smith & Wesson firearm and how those features affect operation or handling.

steps.title: Safety on if fitted, magazine out, slide back and locked open
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger, place the manual safety in SAFE if your pistol has one, press the magazine release and remove the magazine. Starting with the slide closed, grasp its serrated sides from the rear, hold the pistol upright and draw the slide briskly fully rearward to extract anything in the chamber. Pull it fully to the rear, press upward on the slide stop and let the slide move slightly forward so it locks open.
steps.prose: Magazine before chamber, so nothing feeds behind the round you are extracting. The lock-open sequence is press-then-ease-forward: pressing the stop into a moving slide is how the stop and the slide notch get chewed.
steps.quote: Pull the slide fully to the rear, press upward on the slide stop while letting the slide move slightly forward thereby locking the slide open (FIGURE 46).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.30

steps.title: Chamber clear before anything goes into the frame
steps.action: With the slide locked open, make certain the chamber is clear of any ammunition, and look down through the magazine well as well.
steps.prose: This one is not routine box-ticking on a Shield Plus. The very next step puts a screwdriver into the ejection port and pushes a lever down into the magazine well, so the gun has to be verifiably empty before a tool goes anywhere near it.
steps.quote: Make certain that the chamber is clear of any ammunition (FIGURE 47).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.30

steps.title: Nothing marked +P+ goes in this pistol
steps.action: Check the headstamps of what you have been shooting: +P+ ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.prose: The stated objection is that +P+ names no defined pressure limit at all — it is a loader's own marking, so two boxes carrying it can differ widely in what they generate. On a small, light carry pistol the effect of pressure it was not built for is a battered frame and a recoil spring that stops holding the slide closed at the right moment.
steps.quote: “Plus-P-Plus” (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson® firearms. This marking on the ammunition designates that it exceeds established industry standards, but the designation does not represent defined pressure limits and therefore such ammunition may vary significantly as to the pressures generated and could be DANGEROUS.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Ammunition, p.11

steps.title: SHIELD Plus and SHIELD X magazines are not interchangeable
steps.action: Keep your pistol's own magazines with it. The SHIELD Plus grip frame is shorter than the SHIELD X grip frame, and the magazines for the two are not directly interchangeable even though both are covered by this manual.
steps.prose: This is the trap that comes with one book covering two pistols: the magazines look like near relatives and are sold under adjacent part numbers. A SHIELD X magazine in a SHIELD Plus stands proud of the grip and does not present rounds at the right height; the reverse leaves the follower short of the feed lips at the top of the stack.
steps.quote: The grip length of a SHIELD® Plus pistol is shorter than the grip length of the SHIELD X™ pistol (FIGURES 71 through 74). The magazines are not directly interchangeable.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Magazines, NOTE, p.36

steps.title: Push the yellow sear deactivation lever down into the magazine well
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look down through the ejection port for the small yellowish sear deactivation lever toward the rear of the pistol. Use a small screwdriver or similar to push it gently down — rotating it forward — into the magazine well. Do not force the lever down beyond that position.
steps.prose: This is the Shield Plus's signature step and the one people miss: nothing else will let the takedown lever turn, and forcing the takedown lever against an un-lowered sear lever is how both get damaged. Gently and only as far as it goes; the manual prints 'do not force lever down beyond this position' beside its own photograph for a reason.
steps.caution: Do not force lever down beyond this position.
steps.quote: Use a small screwdriver (or a similar device) to gently push the yellow(ish) sear deactivation lever down (rotate forward) into the magazine well (FIGURES 48 and 49).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.31

steps.title: Takedown lever 90 degrees clockwise, then slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Rotate the takedown lever 90 degrees clockwise. Then pull the slide slightly rearward to disengage the slide stop and take the slide forward off the frame, keeping control of the recoil spring and guide rod assembly as it comes free.
steps.prose: Note the direction: clockwise on this pistol, where the EZ and Bodyguard levers go down past six o'clock. The slide comes off with the sear lever still lowered, so do not let go of it and reach for something else halfway through. The recoil spring is compressed the whole way.
steps.quote: Pull the slide slightly rearward to disengage the slide stop and then remove the slide forward from the frame while being careful to retain the recoil spring and guide rod assembly (FIGURE 51).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.31

steps.title: Recoil spring out of the barrel lug groove, then the barrel
steps.action: Remove the recoil spring assembly from below the barrel: compress the rear of the spring forward slightly, lift it up from the rear out of the groove in the barrel lug, and lift it clear of the slide. Then take the barrel out of the bottom of the slide by grasping the lug and lifting up and back.
steps.prose: The spring's rear sits in a groove rather than merely resting against the lug, so it has to be compressed forward before it will lift — pulling straight up just bends it against the lug. The barrel then comes up and back; straight up wedges the lug in the slide's locking recess.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring assembly from below the barrel (FIGURE 52). Compress the rear of the spring forward slightly and lift it up from the rear and out of the groove in the barrel lug. Lift the spring out of the slide and set it aside.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.31

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Grip-frame assembly, slide assembly, barrel, recoil spring assembly and magazine — that is the pistol field stripped, and as far as Smith & Wesson takes it. Leave the sear deactivation lever down until the slide is going back on. Deep Clean covers the magazine, which the manual documents separately.
steps.prose: The lever has to be tipped down again before the slide will reinstall, so putting it back up now only means doing it twice.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE DISASSEMBLY/FIELD STRIPPING PROCEDURE DETAILED IN THIS MANUAL, OR PERFORM ANY MAINTENANCE, ADJUSTMENT, OR SERVICE NOT SPECIFIED.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, WARNING, p.29

deepSteps.title: Identify your floor plate type first
deepSteps.action: Before you take a magazine apart, look at the bottom of it. Type 1 uses a push-button floor plate catch and Type 2 uses a friction-fit catch, and the disassembly is different for each. The steps that follow are the Type 1 push-button procedure.
deepSteps.prose: Getting this wrong is how floor plates get broken — hunting for a button on a friction-fit plate, or levering a push-button plate off without depressing the catch. Look, then choose.
deepSteps.quote: There are basically two types of floor plates found on the various magazines. Type 1 uses a “push-button” floor plate catch and Type 2 uses a “friction-fit” floor plate catch (FIGURE 70).
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Magazines, NOTE ABOUT MAGAZINE TYPE 1 & 2, p.36
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure in the assembled magazine. Control the spring and other parts of the magazine so they do not fly out and cause injury.

deepSteps.title: Type 1: depress the catch through the floor plate hole
deepSteps.action: With the magazine out and empty, use a small diameter tool through the hole in the floor plate to depress the floor plate catch.
deepSteps.prose: The hole is sized for a punch of the right diameter and nothing larger will reach the catch. Keep the magazine pointed away from your face from this point on — a Shield Plus magazine is a high-capacity stack in a small tube and there is real spring energy under that catch.
deepSteps.quote: Using a small diameter tool, depress floor plate catch through the hole in the floor plate (FIGURE 75).
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Type 1 Magazine Disassembly, p.38

deepSteps.title: Floor plate forward, then catch, spring and follower out
deepSteps.action: Slide the floor plate forward off the tube while holding the floor plate catch in the tube against spring pressure, then remove the catch, spring and follower out through the bottom.
deepSteps.prose: Forward is the only direction the plate leaves. Your thumb has to take over from the tool as the plate travels, because the instant the plate stops covering the catch the spring pushes everything out. Clean the inside of the tube while it is open — this is a tightly stacked magazine and residue there is what makes the top rounds sit low.
deepSteps.quote: Slide floor plate forward off of the tube while holding floor plate catch in the tube (FIGURE 76) against spring pressure.
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
FOR S&W® / M&P® SHIELD® PLUS
and M&P® SHIELD X™ — REV:SHIELD_PLUS & SHIELD X_071726 — Type 1 Magazine Disassembly, p.38

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish with a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore to remove residue and solvent
On a ported model, clean the barrel ports and the matching cuts in the slide every time
Clean the feed ramp and the groove in the barrel lug where the recoil spring seats

cleaning.name: SLIDE AND FRAME
tasks: Clean the breech face, the extractor and the inside of the slide
Clean the frame rails and the takedown lever recess
Clean around the sear deactivation lever without prying at it, and check it returns fully up on its own
Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cleaning cloth and remove all solution, oil and fingerprints

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the tube and feed lips; keep SHIELD Plus and SHIELD X magazines separated from each other
If the magazine has been apart, clean the inside of the tube and the follower before reassembly
Check the floor plate is locked by trying gently to slide it forward

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Seven lubrication points, a single drop of high-quality firearm lubricant at each
Do not over-lubricate: excess collects unburned powder and carbon residue and interferes with proper functioning
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this pistol

reassembly: With the bottom of the slide turned up, put the barrel back in so the muzzle is flush with the end of the slide and the barrel lug is turned up away from the ejection port.
Insert the recoil spring assembly muzzle end first and tip its rear into the notch on the barrel lug, then check it is centred and properly seated against the lug.
Make sure the sear deactivation lever is still tipped down (forward) before installing the slide.
Fit the slide onto the frame rails and bring it rearward, lock it open, rotate the takedown lever back 90 degrees into its locked position, then close the slide — the sear lever returns on its own.
Magazine: install the follower, spring and floor plate catch in the orientation they came out, then slide the floor plate rearward onto the tube until the catch locks it.
A ported barrel goes back only into the ported slide it came from.
fncheck: With the pistol empty and pointed in a safe direction, confirm the takedown lever is rotated fully back into its locked position and that the sear deactivation lever has returned to its up position. Cycle the slide by hand several times and check it runs fully into battery and that the slide stop locks it open and releases cleanly. If your pistol has a manual thumb safety, confirm it moves positively between SAFE and FIRE. Then seat an empty magazine of the correct type for your grip length, confirm it latches and drops free, and if your pistol has a magazine disconnect safety confirm the trigger does not release with the magazine removed.
